evidence.note: Systematic, section-by-section reading of RFC 8878 (frame header, blocks, literals, sequences, FSE, Huffman) before writing any code at step 25 — well beyond reactive skimming.
Hand-parsed simple.zst hex dump correctly (magic, descriptor 0x24, FCS width, block type, checksum), grounding the frame-header model in real bytes.
Read Appendix A precomputed FSE tables to ground predefined-mode decoding; but transcribed them with miscounts/off-by-one errors (steps 63-70), showing imperfect extraction of exact rules.
On impossible output, returned to RFC 3.1.1.3.1.1 and correctly diagnosed the Raw/RLE vs Compressed/Treeless Size_Format bit-layout difference — reconciling spec against observed bytes.
Repeated mis-reads of tricky rules: Huffman weight formula (2^(max-w) vs 2^(w-1)) and forward bit-reader MSB-vs-LSB ordering — the field-width/bit-order errors characteristic of lower anchors.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it read the RFC systematically section-by-section before coding and hand-parsed real .zst hex dumps (simple.zst, repetitive.zst) to ground its model, and it repeatedly returned to specific spec sections when debugging. However, it falls short of level 8 because the exact rules for the hardest areas (FSE table build, Huffman weight decoding, bit ordering, Appendix A table contents) were repeatedly mis-extracted and only corrected reactively through debug prints, rather than verified against hex dumps before being trusted. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.
